_note: Transcription of the exact Railway Template Composer settings for the Supabase Self-Hosted template. Railway does NOT read this file automatically — enter these settings in the Template Composer when publishing, and check the published page against this file. Source repo: https://github.com/AdeelAhmedKhan/supabase-selfhost-railway (slim repo: official docker/ plus railway/ adaptation), branch main. Build context for every Dockerfile service is the repo root, so COPY paths are root-relative.

buckets.name: StorageBucket
buckets.note: Railway Bucket, auto-provisioned at deploy. The Storage service references its S3 credentials. Buckets are private; files are served through the storage API, never directly.

category_note: If the composer offers no Databases category, use the closest backend/database category it shows and note the change here.
description: Full Supabase stack in one click: database, auth, storage, Studio
deviationsFromOfficial: ENABLE_EMAIL_AUTOCONFIRM is true (official default false) so signup works on first run without an SMTP server. Add SMTP and flip it to false for production.
Storage backend is a Railway Bucket (S3) instead of a local disk volume.
No shared volume between Storage and Imgproxy (Railway volumes attach to one service only).
Studio's edge-functions folder is an empty volume in v1; functions code lives in the Functions image.
Gateway listens on an explicit PORT=8000 so public and private traffic use the same port.
name: Supabase Self-Hosted
notIncluded: Logs and analytics services (separate official overlay, not the base compose)
SMTP email sending (configure post-deploy; signup works without it because autoconfirm is on by default, see deviations)
Custom domain setup (add your domain to the gateway service after deploy)
Backups (snapshot the Postgres volume or schedule dumps)
Asymmetric sb_ API keys (optional follow-up per official docs; this template runs legacy HS256 keys)

build.note: Railway builds this image at deploy time from the fork. The entrypoint derives ANON_KEY and SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from JWT_SECRET, builds the Envoy config from the official templates, points backend clusters at Railway private domains, and prints the Supabase URL and anon key to the deploy log.

healthcheck.note: Envoy admin lives on 127.0.0.1:9901 inside the container and is not public. Health is proven by the gateway answering on its public domain after deploy (first deploy check), not by process liveness alone.

ANON_KEY_ASYMMETRIC.note: Empty: legacy-only mode. Asymmetric sb_ keys are an optional follow-up per official docs.

AUTH_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the auth cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

DASHBOARD_PASSWORD.note: Generated at deploy time. Dashboard login password; find it in the Gateway service Variables tab after deploy.

FUNCTIONS_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the functions cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

JWT_SECRET.note: Generated at deploy time, defined ONCE here, referenced by every other service. Never generate it per service or authentication breaks.

META_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the meta cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

PORT.note: Explicit 8000 so public traffic and private traffic use the same gateway port. Verify the composer accepts this override at publish time.

REALTIME_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the realtime cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

REST_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the rest cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

STORAGE_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the storage cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

STUDIO_HOST.note: Railway reference variable. Used by the gateway entrypoint to rewrite the studio cluster endpoint in cds.yaml.

SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL.note: Self-reference to the gateway public domain. Verify the composer accepts it; if it rejects self-reference, leave this empty on Gateway and keep the cross-service references.

build.note: FROM supabase/postgres:17.6.1.136 plus the four official init scripts copied into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/. The postgresql.conf comes from the image itself.

healthcheck.note: Database services have no HTTP healthcheck path. Health is proven by an authenticated psql connection, not by process liveness alone.

PGSODIUM_ROOT_KEY.note: Generated at deploy time, defined here. Never change it after the first deploy unless following the upstream rotation guide.

POSTGRES_HOST.note: Official db-service value: local socket path inside this container.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.note: Generated at deploy time, defined ONCE here, referenced by every other service. Never change it after the first deploy unless following the upstream rotation guide.

volumes.note: Persistent volume. Without it, all data is lost on redeploy.

build.note: FROM supabase/studio:2026.10.12-sha-3699278 plus an entrypoint that derives SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY from JWT_SECRET at startup.

EDGE_FUNCTIONS_MANAGEMENT_FOLDER.note: Empty volume in v1: functions code lives in the Functions image, so Studio's Functions browser shows an empty folder. Functions still run at /functions/v1/<name>.

ENABLED_FEATURES_LOGS_ALL.note: Official default: logs services are not part of this template.

OPENAI_API_KEY.note: Optional. Leave empty unless you want Studio's AI features.

SNIPPETS_MANAGEMENT_FOLDER.note: Backed by the snippets volume below.

STUDIO_PG_META_URL.note: Railway reference variable plus the meta internal port.

SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.note: DO NOT SET in the composer. Derived at container start by the Studio entrypoint from JWT_SECRET.

SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY.note: DO NOT SET in the composer. Derived at container start by the Studio entrypoint from JWT_SECRET.

SUPABASE_URL.note: Railway reference variable plus the gateway internal port.

volumes.note: Saved SQL snippets persist across redeploys.
Empty in v1 (see EDGE_FUNCTIONS_MANAGEMENT_FOLDER note). Guarantees the directory exists so Studio does not error.

API_EXTERNAL_URL.note: Railway reference variable plus the auth path, matching the official .env.example shape.

GOTRUE_DB_DATABASE_URL.note: Railway reference variables. The auth admin database user is created by the official db init scripts.

GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_PHONE_ENABLED.note: Phone signup off by default; needs an SMS provider.

GOTRUE_JWT_ISSUER.note: Matches API_EXTERNAL_URL, as in official compose.

GOTRUE_MAILER_AUTOCONFIRM.note: DEVIATION from official default (false): true so signup works on first run without an SMTP server. Add SMTP and flip this to false for production.

GOTRUE_SITE_URL.note: Starts as the gateway URL. Change this to your app URL after deploy so auth emails and redirects point at your app.

GOTRUE_URI_ALLOW_LIST.note: Empty by default. Add your app URLs here (comma separated) when you connect an app.

PGRST_DB_URI.note: Railway reference variables. The authenticator database user is created by the official db init scripts.

PGRST_JWT_SECRET.note: Railway reference variable. Legacy mode: the raw secret, not a JWKS.

DB_ENC_KEY.note: Railway reference variable to the generated key on this same service.

REALTIME_DB_ENC_KEY.note: Generated at deploy time, defined here. Must be exactly 16 hex characters; Railway generation plus the entrypoint does not enforce length, so verify the generated value length at publish time.

SECRET_KEY_BASE.note: Generated at deploy time, defined ONCE here, referenced by Supavisor.

build.note: FROM supabase/storage-api:v1.81.0 plus an entrypoint that derives ANON_KEY and SERVICE_KEY from JWT_SECRET at startup.

ANON_KEY.note: DO NOT SET in the composer. Derived at container start by the Storage entrypoint from JWT_SECRET.

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.note: Railway reference variable to the StorageBucket credentials.

AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.note: Railway reference variable to the StorageBucket credentials.

FILE_STORAGE_BACKEND_PATH.note: Official default. Unused with the S3 backend, kept for compatibility.

GLOBAL_S3_BUCKET.note: Railway reference variable to the StorageBucket name.

GLOBAL_S3_ENDPOINT.note: Railway reference variable to the StorageBucket endpoint. Verify the endpoint format (full URL vs host) at first live deploy.

GLOBAL_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE.note: Railway Buckets use virtual-hosted style URLs, so path style stays off.

IMGPROXY_URL.note: Railway reference variable plus the imgproxy internal port.

POSTGREST_URL.note: Railway reference variable plus the REST internal port.

REGION.note: Railway reference variable to the StorageBucket region.

S3_PROTOCOL_ACCESS_KEY_ID.note: Generated at deploy time, defined here. These are storage-api's own S3-protocol credentials, separate from the backend bucket credentials.

S3_PROTOCOL_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET.note: Generated at deploy time, defined here.

SERVICE_KEY.note: DO NOT SET in the composer. Derived at container start by the Storage entrypoint from JWT_SECRET.

STORAGE_BACKEND.note: s3: files live in the Railway Bucket, not on a local disk.

IMGPROXY_LOCAL_FILESYSTEM_ROOT.note: Official default. No shared volume in v1: the image-transformation fetch path is untested, see stillUntestedAtPublish.

CRYPTO_KEY.note: Railway reference variable to the generated key on this same service.

PG_META_CRYPTO_KEY.note: Generated at deploy time, defined here, referenced by Studio.

build.note: FROM supabase/edge-runtime:v1.77.4 plus an entrypoint that derives SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from JWT_SECRET at startup, plus the official functions directory (main worker and hello example) copied into /home/deno/functions/.

SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.note: DO NOT SET in the composer. Derived at container start by the Functions entrypoint from JWT_SECRET.

SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.note: DO NOT SET in the composer. Derived at container start by the Functions entrypoint from JWT_SECRET.

SUPABASE_URL.note: Railway reference variable plus the gateway internal port.

VERIFY_JWT.note: Official default: false. Flip to true on Functions when you want every function call to require a valid JWT.

build.note: FROM supabase/supavisor:2.9.13 plus the official pooler.exs copied to /etc/pooler/pooler.exs. The start command (set in the Dockerfile CMD) migrates, evaluates the pooler config, then starts the server.

POOLER_TENANT_ID.note: Replaces the official placeholder. Any consistent identifier works; apps connect as postgres.<tenant>.

POOLER_URL_TRANSACTION.note: Reference variable for apps on Railway that want pooled connections. Verify the 6543 port at first live deploy; supavisor PORT=4000 is its internal API port, not the pooler port.

VAULT_ENC_KEY.note: Generated at deploy time, defined here.

stillUntestedAtPublish: Live Railway deploy of this template (waits for a paid Railway plan to be active).
Storage S3 endpoint format (full URL vs host) against the Railway Bucket.
Gateway PORT override behavior for public and private traffic.
Inter-service private-domain ports (all services on their official internal ports).
Imgproxy image-transformation fetch path without a shared storage volume.
Functions main worker boot with the official main/index.ts and hello example.
First-run cost: 11 services plus a bucket. Watch one day of usage before judging.
verifyAtPublish: Gateway self-reference SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL=${{Gateway.RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN}} is accepted by the composer; if rejected, leave it empty on Gateway and keep the cross-service references.
PORT=8000 explicit on Gateway is accepted (edge and private traffic both on 8000).
Bucket reference variables resolve: BUCKET, ENDPOINT, ACCESS_KEY_ID, SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, REGION.
Dockerfile paths resolve with repo-root build context: railway/services/gateway, studio, storage, functions, db, supavisor.
Service names match every ${{...}} reference exactly; a composer rename breaks references.
REALTIME_DB_ENC_KEY generated value is 16 hex characters; VAULT_ENC_KEY and PG_META_CRYPTO_KEY meet their minimum lengths.
